summary: Redwood AE+SE ran a POC scoping call with Sterling Care to agree success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and a quality evaluation plan. Primary goals: define golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, and scoring approach. Security and data residency questions were raised; next steps include benchmarks, docs exchange, and scheduling a private deployment deep dive.
questions: What latency SLOs do you need for primary workflows?
Can you provide a 50-example golden prompt set and an anonymized sample dataset?
Do you require Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment or is Dedicated acceptable?
What are your strictest data residency/KMS requirements?
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - Jordan Meyers, AE. Priya from the SE team will cover the eval plan.
[00:32] Marcus (Sterling): Hi, Marcus here. We're looking to validate accuracy on our clinical summarization flow and make sure hallucinations are under control. Typical volume is around 10k tokens/day to start, could spike to 50k.
[01:05] Priya (Redwood SE): Cool, thanks Marcus. So the goal of today's call is to scope the POC quality eval plan - golden prompts, regression harness, hallucination and format checks, and metrics. I'll run through a proposed approach then we can adjust.
[01:40] Ana (Product): Quick ask - we need the outputs to be deterministic in format: JSON with fields diag_summary, key_actions, and confidence. If the model hallucinates a medication, that's a blocker.
[02:05] Devon (Security): From security side we need to confirm SOC 2 posture, KMS support for keys, SAML/SSO for console access, and whether Private/VPC is possible.
[02:40] Jordan: We'll cover that - Redwood has Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options. For this POC we usually do baseline on Hosted with redwood-verified models then run Dedicated/Private tests for latency and network isolation checks.
[03:10] Priya: Proposed eval plan: 1) Golden prompts - a set of 50 canonical examples you'll provide; 2) Regression tests - a suite of ~500 examples split by template; 3) Hallucination checks - automated heuristics + a 5% human audit sample; 4) Format checks - strict schema validation on JSON outputs; 5) Scoring - a combined score: exact/field match for structured fields + semantic similarity for free-text, plus hallucination penalty.
[04:00] Marcus: That seems reasonable. What thresholds are realistic?
[04:12] Priya: For structured fields we aim for >92% exact-match on golden prompts. For free-text summaries we use embedding similarity (cosine) with a threshold and spot human checks; overall hallucination rate targeted <3% for critical fields.
[04:35] Ana: How do you measure hallucination automatically?
[04:40] Priya: We run entity extraction on model output and compare against source EHR entities; mismatched named entities trigger potential hallucination flags, plus we have heuristics for fabricated medication names and improbable timestamps. Then we surface flagged items to human reviewers.
[05:10] Devon: Are you logging token-level traces? We need audit logs for compliance.
[05:15] Jordan: Yes, Console includes token-level cost and latency traces; for Private/Dedicated we can ship richer audit logs and integrate with your SIEM.
[05:40] Marcus: About workload sizing - our steady is 10k tokens/day, peak 50k. Latency targets: sub-1s for single-turn queries, 1-2s for multi-turn summarization if possible.
[06:05] Priya: Ok for benchmarks we'll run three profiles: small (5k/day), mid (10k/day), large (50k/day) and produce latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll test 3 model variants: redwood-curated small, medium, and a quantized variant on Dedicated to see cost tradeoffs.
[06:40] Marcus: Do you support KV cache and continuous batching? That affects latency.
[06:45] Priya: Yes, runtime supports KV cache and continuous batching. We'll include tests with and without KV cache to show cold-start vs warm-case latency. Also test quantized weights to measure degradation in quality.
[07:15] Ana: For the golden prompts, we will send 50 examples but many contain PHI. We'll anonymize, but expect Redwood to support private handling.
[07:34] Devon: On that note, we need to confirm KMS/HSM details and whether keys stay in our tenant.
[07:45] Jordan: For Private deployment keys can remain in your KMS. For Hosted/Dedicated we offer KMS integrations - we'll follow up with our security doc.
[08:10] Marcus: How do you do regression tests across model versions?
[08:15] Priya: We maintain a regression harness that runs golden prompts and full regression set across candidate model versions. Results include per-example diffs, score deltas, and flagged regressions when quality falls below thresholds. We also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous version if regression is detected.
[08:50] Marcus: Good. What's the scoring formula?
[08:55] Priya: Example: structured fields (diag_summary.key_actions) weighted 60% by exact-match; free text summary weighted 30% by embedding similarity and rouge-like measures; hallucination penalty weighted 10% (applied as subtraction). Composite score out of 100, pass if >90 on golden prompts and no critical hallucinations.
[09:30] Ana: Will you provide the scripts for running the harness?
[09:35] Priya: Yes - we'll share a reproducible benchmark repo with instructions and a prebuilt docker that runs the harness against the API or Private endpoint.
[10:02] Devon: SAML/SSO and RBAC - can Redwood map to our IdP and apply role restrictions per team?
[10:08] Jordan: Yes, we support SAML SSO and role-based access controls in Console. We'll include docs and a setup guide.
[10:30] Marcus: Timelines?
[10:33] Jordan: Proposed: this week gather golden prompts and sample data; Priya runs baseline benchmarks within 5 business days; by week two we run Dedicated/Private tests and deliver a full eval report. So about 2 weeks to a comprehensive POC report.
[11:00] Priya: For hallucination/format checks we'll produce automated reports: per-example status (pass/fail), hallucination flags, confidence scores, and a human-reviewed sample that covers edge cases. We'll also export examples that changed between model versions for triage.
[11:40] Marcus: What's the expected human review load?
[11:45] Priya: We suggest a 5-10% human audit on flagged items initially - we'll sample across templates. That gives good coverage without overwhelming your reviewers.
[12:05] Ana: For format validation, if the model returns malformed JSON, do you have auto-correction or do you mark fail?
[12:12] Priya: The harness will attempt minor repairs (like trailing commas) and count as tolerable if structure can be recovered; but if critical fields are missing or types wrong it's a fail. We'll include both strict and lenient modes in the report.
[12:40] Devon: Any concerns about PII retention in Hosted?
[12:45] Jordan: By default Hosted retains minimal logs; for sensitive data we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can control retention and keys. We'll detail retention policies in the security pack.
[13:10] Marcus: Ok let's talk benchmarks specifics - what metrics will you return?
[13:15] Priya: We'll return p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, success-rate on format validation, exact-match rates for structured fields, embedding-similarity stats for summaries, hallucination rate. We'll also provide per-model comparison charts.
[13:50] Ana: Will you score per-workflow SLA?
[13:54] Priya: Yes we'll produce per-route dashboards and a composite score aligned to your success criteria.
[14:20] Jordan: Any blockers to proceed?
[14:23] Marcus: We need to finalize the golden prompts and confirm anonymization approach. Also security needs the KMS/HSM answers.
[14:35] Jordan: Action items then: Marcus to send prompts and sample data; Devon to send security constraints; Priya runs benchmarks once data's in.
[14:55] Devon: One more - can you show results on quantized models? We want cost/perf tradeoffs.
[15:00] Priya: Yes we'll include a quantized variant and measure quality drop; also run with different kernel choices where applicable.
[15:25] Marcus: If a model shows regression we'll want a rollback path.
[15:30] Priya: We'll set up canary rollouts and automatic fallback; the harness supports gating rules.
[15:50] Ana: Sounds good. Any last questions?
[15:55] Marcus: Not right now.
[15:58] Jordan: Great - recap of next steps and deliverables on the thread, we'll follow up with security and pricing docs. Thanks everyone.
[56:00] -- End of recording (note: timestamp aligns with declared duration)
